title: Configuring Scan Rule for Azure Container Registry (ACR) Repositories

blocks.text: You can configure the scan rule to discover vulnerabilities and software packages within your container images stored in Azure Container Registry (ACR). AI Security detects vulnerabilities, AI Models, AI Packages, and MCP servers.

Before you configure a scan rule, ensure you have enabled the Azure Container Registry service within the product's Manage Services settings. This tells the system that you want it to discover and scan container registries in your Azure environment. To learn more, see Managing Services. You must also ensure you have executed the latest Azure onboarding templates that include the necessary IAM permissions for ACR scanning. To learn more, see IAM Roles and Permissions for Azure.
To enable scanning of a private Azure Container Registry (ACR) from a scanner instance, two network-level configurations are required:

blocks.item: VNet Peering (Bidirectional): The customer must establish a VNet peering between the scanner VNet and the VNet where the private ACR is deployed. Without peering, scanner traffic cannot reach the address space where the ACR private endpoint lives.

Private DNS Zone VNet Link: The customer must link the scanner VNet to the Private DNS Zone where the ACR private endpoint DNS records are registered— this ensures the scanner can resolve the ACR hostname to its private IP.

blocks.text: If the ACR has IP network rules configured, the scanner's outbound IPs must be explicitly whitelisted.
To configure a scan rule for ACR container image repositories, complete the following steps in the AI Security Admin Portal:

blocks.item: 1. Provide the general information.
Go to Administration > Scan Settings.
Select the Scan Rules tab.
Click Add Scan Rule.
See image.
The General Information page appears.
On the General Information page:
Scan Rule Name: Enter a unique and descriptive name for the scan rule.
Scan Rule Description (Optional): Enter a description for the scan rule (maximum is 500 characters).
See image.
Click Next.
2. Select the cloud and resource type.
On the Select Cloud and Resource Type page:
For Cloud Type, select Azure.
For Resource Type, select Container Image Repositories.
Click Next.
3. Select the subscriptions that must be scanned.
On the Select the Resources to Scan page, choose one of the following options:
Scan All Resources: Scans all discovered repositories across all onboarded subscriptions.
See image.
Scan Specific Resources: Scan all subscriptions and its associated registries and resources. When you select this option, select the checkbox for the repositories that must be scanned.
Select Specific Subscriptions and Regions: Select the checkbox for specific subscriptions and regions that must be scanned.
Scan Specific Registries: Specify the registries for scanning.
Select from the List: Select the checkbox for the ACR registries that must be scanned.
Scan Specific Repositories: Specify the repositories that must be scanned. Enter the repository name manually or in the regex format, e.g., dev* or prod*.
Select Repositories: Select the checkbox for the repositories that must be scanned. Enter the repository names manually or in the regex format, e.g., dev* or prod*.
Select by Image Tags: Specify the tags in key-value pairs. All the ACR repositories that match the tag are scanned.

If multiple key-value pairs are added, AI Security scans all container registries that match at least one of the specified key-value pairs. This means the rule uses OR logic, and a registry is included if it matches any of the specified tags.
See image.
If you choose Scan All Resources, or Scan Specific Resources, you can optionally exclude specific ACR repositories from the scan.
In the Scan by Last Pulled option, select a timeframe to only scan images that have been pulled within that period.
Click Next.
4. Exclude ACR repositories (Optional).
On the Exclude ACR Repositories (Optional) page, you can specify the ACR repositories that must be excluded from the scan.
If a full scan is already initiated or completed, the ACR repositories are excluded in the next incremental scan.
Enter the ACR repositories names separated by commas.
See image.
Click Next.
5. Set up the scan schedule.
On the Scan Schedule page, select the scan frequency:
On Demand (Default): Scan the data manually when needed.
Daily: Scan the data daily.
Weekly: Scan the data once a week. Select the day from the drop-down menu.
Monthly: Scan the data once a month.
See image.
Click Next.
6. Review and complete the configuration.
Review the scan rule. Click the Edit icon to change any values, if required.
See image.
Click Finish.
